stories.notes: Story has empty acceptance criteria and no existing spec (spec: null). Complex multi-market CMS live preview feature requiring full requirements elaboration first (openspec), then testability/security/edge-case hardening (speckit). Openspec runs first to define ACs and technical depth; speckit reviews and hardens the output. No hand-curated spec detected, so both agents are warranted.

agentContributions.notes: Live Preview is a novel capability — no preview mechanism exists in the current useContent hook or ContentstackContext. Attachment points are the content-fetching hook and the context/provider layer. Verification criteria are derived from the description since acceptance criteria are empty; they stop at the Contentstack boundary (unreachable at test time) and assert observable rendering behavior given mocked preview data.

Openspec provided empty acceptance criteria, so all criteria are derived from the story title/description and the listed file paths. File contents were NOT available for review — criteria assume a standard Contentstack Live Preview integration pattern (WebSocket/polling-based real-time updates via the SDK, with a preview token and content delivery vs. content management API distinction). If the actual implementation differs significantly (e.g., iframe-based preview, different SDK), some criteria may need adjustment. AC-1 through AC-3 cover the core happy path and mode toggle. AC-4 through AC-6 cover error handling and fallback. AC-7 and AC-8 cover concurrency and lifecycle edge cases. AC-9 and AC-13 cover reference/link resolution in preview mode. AC-10 covers the no-preview-config baseline. AC-11 covers editor disconnect. AC-12 covers loading state observability. AC-14 covers interface mismatch resilience.

coordinatorReview.reviewNotes: Both agents ran but acceptance criteria remain empty (acceptanceChanged: false on both, splitCount: 0). Speckit's notes reference AC-1 through AC-14, but none were persisted into the story's acceptanceCriteria array. Openspec derived criteria from the title/description but did not write them; speckit then reviewed criteria that don't exist in the record. Speckit also admits file contents were unavailable, meaning all 14 referenced criteria are assumption-based against a standard Contentstack integration pattern that may not match the actual implementation. For a complex multi-market CMS live preview feature, zero story splits and empty acceptance criteria after a full pipeline run is a failure state. Human intervention is required to either (a) re-run the pipeline with file context available so agents can produce and persist real criteria, or (b) hand-curate acceptance criteria before re-running speckit for hardening.
